title: Formal Prepositional Phrases for Describing a City

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *mediante* from B1 Unit 24 ("by means of"), and *debido a* and *a raíz de* from B1 Unit 6. These formal phrases are followed directly by a noun, and they let you explain how a city was built and why it changed.

sections.title: Means and cause in the story of a city
rows: Mediante el relleno con escombros se ganó tierra al río.
Debido a la poca profundidad, los barcos anclaban lejos.
*debido a* + noun: because of the shallow water
A raíz del tamaño de los barcos, se hizo un puerto nuevo.
*a raíz de* + noun: as a result of the size of the ships
Mediante estas avenidas, la ciudad se parecía a París.
*mediante* often opens a sentence, followed by a comma

items.spanish: Mediante el relleno con escombros, se ganó tierra al río.
items.english: By means of landfill, land was won from the river.

items.spanish: Debido a la poca profundidad de la costa, los barcos grandes anclaban lejos.
items.english: Because of the shallow coast, big ships anchored far away.

items.spanish: A raíz del tamaño de los barcos, Puerto Madero quedó pequeño.
items.english: As a result of the size of the ships, Puerto Madero became too small.

items.spanish: Mediante nuevos parques y avenidas, la ciudad cambió de aspecto.
items.english: By means of new parks and avenues, the city changed its look.

sections.content: After *mediante*, *debido a* and *a raíz de* put a noun, not a verb: *debido a la poca profundidad*. With *el*, *a* + *el* becomes *al* and *de* + *el* becomes *del*: *a raíz del tamaño*. Do not say *mediante de* or *debido de*.
